title: Are there workflows available for generating art for an isometric tiled game?
author: Soberocean1
selftext: I've been working with codex and pixel lab to try get assets generated to match the grid exactly but they always come off not straight and an awkward height. Has anyone figured out any workflows to make stuff fit correctly?

comments.author: LegoFighter2
comments.body: not really. you can check my repo [https://github.com/LegoFighter/heart-of-the-light](https://github.com/LegoFighter/heart-of-the-light) and prompt against the code

comments.author: PositiveScarcity8909
comments.body:
This is making me dizzy lol

Maybe try generation the assets tile a tile from modular parts?

AI will have an easier time creating a straight line inside 1 cell.

replies.author: Soberocean1
replies.body: Yep looks awful aha everytime I tried improving it I made it worse

comments.author: freqCake
comments.body:
Make 3d models, render in blender with an orthographic camera, use the same camera angle and position for every single render, have a grid layer on blender you can enable to see if its misaligned with the grid, have the rotational pivot point for the models be the center of the tile so you can rotate them 90 degrees at a time to catch each angle

This way you have a reproducible stage to render all your models on, and its a simple workflow to rotate the model to get all the angles problematically (and alignment with the grid is the only real task)

replies.author: Soberocean1
replies.body: This sound like a good solution, I'll give this a go, thanks

comments.author: Shrineheart
comments.body: Isometric/Diametric can be difficult for AI to do. I do my art by hand but I've swapped to 3d modeling in Blockbench of all things and then using a filter to get the desired look in game. Also allows for full 360 turn arounds too.

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body: i gave up, made blueprints in photoshop and now i copy EVERY asset by hand into photoshop and scale and transform it and then let ai export layers from photoshop files and it works perfect, i just wish i wouldnt have to do such a mundane piece of  work myself but i guess 2027  its a piece of cake for any agent

comments.author: matt_williamson
comments.body: I've been getting much better results by uploading an isometric template image to work from. Just a neutral gray diamond.

replies.author: matt_williamson
replies.body:
I created a PNG with a transparent background and a 2:1 grey diamond. The exact shape for an isometric floor tile. I attach it to the prompt and type something like, "Use this template to render a isometric...". From that the AI (Gemini) usually keeps the shape correct. It was always askew before this.

Even my corrals came out "square": [https://cheerychimp.com/hollow-farm/](https://cheerychimp.com/hollow-farm/)
